caption: Figure 2. Synthetic final task success and independent run variation at epoch 30. (a) Bars show the arithmetic mean and error bars plus or minus one sample SD (n−1 denominator) across six synthetic runs per method, with a zero-based 0–100% vertical scale. Means ± SD are 57.881 ± 0.866% for Baseline, 69.476 ± 1.252% for Context, and 79.048 ± 1.308% for Proposed. (b) All 18 original endpoint values are shown once against their seed IDs on an explicitly expanded 50–85% vertical scale. Gray circles, orange triangles and blue squares retain the Baseline, Context and Proposed roles used in Figure 1. Seed labels identify runs and do not establish cross-method pairing; no points are connected. These endpoint values exactly match the epoch-30 observations in the learning table. SD describes run-to-run variation, not a confidence interval for generalization. No values were excluded and no significance analysis was added. All results are Synthetic demonstrations.
alt_text: Synthetic final-results figure with two horizontal panels. Left: zero-baseline bars compare mean task success with sample SD error bars across six runs per method. Baseline is about 57.9 percent, Context 69.5 percent and Proposed 79.0 percent. Right: eighteen unconnected points show all six seed-labeled runs per method on a 50 to 85 percent scale. Baseline gray circles range from 56.337 to 58.904 percent, Context orange triangles from 67.671 to 71.353 percent, and Proposed blue squares from 77.382 to 80.181 percent. A three-marker legend identifies methods. Proposed has the highest mean in these Synthetic data.
